paperTitle: A Deep Learning Assisted Pipeline for Pixel Art Sprite Generation
centralContribution: This paper presents a deep-learning-assisted technique for generating pixel art sprites from line art sketches, aiming to reduce asset-making costs and time in game development. It proposes a novel variant of the Pix2Pix architecture to automatically convert line art into gray (shaded) and color sprites, demonstrating its effectiveness within the production pipeline of a 2D pixel-art fighting game, Trajes Fatais: Suits of Fate.

units.title: Paper Abstract
units.summary: Automated pixel art sprite generation via deep learning for game development.

content.description: The paper introduces a deep-learning pipeline for generating pixel art sprites from line art, reducing game asset creation costs. It utilizes a modified Pix2Pix architecture to produce gray and color sprites, validated in a 2D fighting game production.

units.whyThisUnit: Provides a quick overview of the paper's aim, method, and context, serving as an initial entry point for understanding.

content.description: Creating pixel art sprites manually is time-consuming, with shading alone taking 30-40 minutes per sprite. This bottleneck significantly increases game development costs and time, justifying the need for automated solutions.

Quantitative analysis using RMSE, MAE, and SSIM metrics showed that generated gray sprites performed significantly better and were visually more similar to ground truth than color ones. Color* results, while worse in mean error, showed reduced error standard deviation for color deviation.
